title: Evolution of Log-Based Detection Rules in Public Repositories
abstract: arXiv:2605.05383v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Log-based detection rules remain central to modern security operations, encoding domain expertise that analysts iteratively refine to balance detection coverage against alert volume. Yet while prior work has examined the evolution of network intrusion detection signatures, the longitudinal behavior of log-based detection rules has received little empirical study. We present the first longitudinal analysis of detection rule evolution across two widely used repositories: the community-driven Sigma project and the curated Splunk Security Content (SSC). To compare rule versions based on detection logic rather than surface syntax, we introduce a predicate graph intermediate representation that canonicalizes the logical structure of a rule, together with a tree alignment procedure for analyzing changes across revisions. translated_title: 公共仓库中基于日志的检测规则演变
translated_abstract: 基于日志的检测规则仍然是现代安全运营的核心，它们编码了领域专业知识，分析师会迭代地完善这些规则，以在检测覆盖率和警报量之间取得平衡。然而，尽管先前的研究已经考察了网络入侵检测签名的演变，但基于日志的检测规则的长期行为却很少得到实证研究。我们首次对两个广泛使用的仓库中的检测规则演变进行了纵向分析：社区驱动的Sigma项目和精心策划的Splunk安全内容（SSC）。为了基于检测逻辑而非表面语法比较规则版本，我们引入了一种谓词图中间表示，它规范化了规则的逻辑结构，并采用树对齐程序来分析各修订版本之间的变化。我们将此方法应用于Sigma和SSC的6,859条规则历史，发现大约56%的规则经历了至少一次修改。
tldr: 本文首次对Sigma和SSC仓库中6,859条基于日志的检测规则进行了纵向分析，通过引入谓词图中间表示和树对齐方法，揭示了约56%的规则在演变过程中经历了修改，为理解检测规则的长期演化提供了新视角。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first longitudinal analysis of 6,859 log-based detection rules from Sigma and SSC repositories, introducing a predicate graph intermediate representation and tree alignment method to reveal that approximately 56% of rules undergo at least one revision.
